text:
Judd Caulfield took the long road. A fifth-round pick of Pittsburgh in 2019, he spent three seasons with Anaheim's AHL team in San Diego before sticking with the Ducks this fall, at 25. NHL.com's Rookie Watch put it simply: he is "earning trust." His ice time has climbed by about two and a half minutes a night over his last ten games, to roughly 15.

He plays a heavy game. At 6'3" and 220 pounds he has 68 hits in 19 games, and he goes to the dangerous areas: his expected goals, the quality of his chances, add up to 5.61, high for a player with only 22 shots. He has converted 4 of them, which is fewer goals than those chances usually produce, even though his shooting percentage looks healthy. Ten points, four on the power play, is a solid first month and a half for a depth winger.

There is no NHL history to lean on, and our talent range for him is wide for that reason. What we'd watch is whether the chances keep coming as his minutes grow. If they do, the goals tend to follow.
headline: Judd Caulfield is a 25-year-old rookie earning his minutes
